summary:
I've been running a home server stack with a personal AI agent (Hermes-Agent), and most of the interesting work lately has been in the plumbing that keeps everything else from stepping on each other. I've got one GPU serving six different jobs — image generation, a couple of chat models, a roleplay backend — so I wrote Switchboard, a proxy that evicts whichever backend is idle, waits for the card to actually free up, then loads whoever's next in line. The harder problem was getting two people talking to the same model at once instead of queueing behind each other: I swapped in a server that does continuous batching and ran it head to head against the old setup — two simultaneous requests finished in roughly the time one used to take alone, instead of one waiting on the other to clear.

On BudgetTracker, a finance tracker I run for myself, I built a set of read-only tools that let the agent answer questions like "how's my cash flow this week" straight from the database instead of guessing off chat history. The daily spending summary pulls yesterday's totals and a two-week run rate as exact numbers from SQL first, then hands only the wording to the model — the agent narrates, it doesn't do the arithmetic. That split surfaced a few real date-handling bugs in the queries that would have quietly produced wrong numbers if I'd let the model compute them itself.

I've also been tinkering on the hardware side. A couch-presence sensor — pause the TV automatically when someone leaves the room — started as a camera doing computer vision, which turned out to be unreliable in practice (lighting, angles, false triggers), so I swapped it for an mmWave radar sensor that just measures motion and distance directly instead of trying to interpret an image. The camera didn't go to waste — it's now repurposed into a barbell rep counter that counts reps on-device with no machine learning involved at all.

Smaller thing worth mentioning: the "recent work" tile on this dashboard is itself produced by a scheduled Claude run that reads my own notes and writes a summary like this one — a small closed loop I set up mostly because it was a convenient way to keep the site honest about what I actually did that week.

highlights.oneLiner: Added continuous batching so two concurrent requests finish in the time one used to take
Read-only agent tools pull cash-flow/spending numbers from SQL instead of guessing
Swapped unreliable camera-based presence detection for mmWave radar
Repurposed the old presence camera into an on-device barbell rep counter, no ML
